Visa Stop Payment Service (VSPS) allows issuers, on behalf of their cardholders, to stop unwanted future payments from debiting an account. Examples of payments that may be stopped include subscriptions or membership fees that a merchant continues to charge despite a cardholder’s attempts to cancel.

Participating issuers place stop instructions in the portfolio file (PF) in the V.I.P. cardholder database (CDB). If acquirers submit a VSPS eligible transaction, V.I.P. checks the database, and if it encounters a stop instruction for that account number, it declines the request. There are three implementation options for Visa Stop Payment Service (VSPS) that can be combined to suit clients' needs:
VSPS user interface through Visa Online (VOL) APIs on Visa Developer Host Implementation with VisaNet Integrated Payment (VIP)

The Visa-recommended implementation option for a fast implementation is the VSPS user interface. Access to optional reporting is available for all implementation options through the VSPS user interface.

These are the VSPS Stop Payment messages. 0302: File Maintenance Request—Only format 2 of the 0302 file maintenance request is valid for accessing or for updating the portfolio file. Field 91 — File Update Code indicates the action required by the issuer: add, delete, replace, or inquire. Field 101—File Name must be present and must contain the file name PF for VSPS updates. 0312: File Maintenance Response—This message is the response to an 0302 file maintenance request. If V.I.P. does not find a matching stop instruction, it continues with normal request processing. A value of 4 in Field 44.1 — Response Source/Reason Code in responses and in issuer advices indicates STIP action. 0120 and 0220 STIP advices include the value 9201 in Field 63.4 — STIP/Switch Reason Code. If V.I.P. encounters a stop instruction, it routes the request to STIP. STIP declines the request, using the response code (R0, R1, or R3) from the portfolio file record as the response in Field 39 — Response Code. These are the type of stop instructions and corresponding response codes.

VSPS Stop Instruction ID: The VSPS stop instruction ID is the unique reference for each stop instruction. The value is generated by V.I.P. and must be provided for inquiry, replace, and delete. VSPS Stop Restrictions: Stop restrictions can be optionally included in merchant level stop instructions to limit the range of transactions to be stopped. These stop restrictions are available:

Field 4 — Amount, Transaction: If the amount is present in the stop instruction, eligible transactions can only be stopped for that amount. If amount is not present, eligible transactions can be stopped for any amount. Field 18 — Merchant Category Code: If an MCC is present in the stop instruction, eligible transactions can only be stopped if they contain that MCC. If MCC is not present in the stop instruction, eligible transaction can be stopped for any MCC.

Maintaining message integrity is critical to V.I.P. full service processing. Message integrity assures V.I.P. full service participants other participants have followed Visa processing rules and a participant can act on a message or a transaction as defined—for instance, a completed transaction was actually completed and a cancelled transaction was, in fact, cancelled. Ensuring message integrity requires participants keep track of incoming and outgoing messages and generate reversals for transactions that cannot be completed. This process involves concepts of transaction tracing, transaction control, and transaction sets. Transaction tracing can be accomplished by using the message type and one or more other key data elements to match request and response messages, to match reversals to original transactions, and to tie a transaction, such as a dispute financial, to the original transaction. Key data elements include:
Transmission date and time. System trace audit number. Transaction identifier (TID). Acquiring institution ID. Retrieval reference number. Original data elements.

V.I.P. assigns a transaction identifier (TID) in field 62.2 to all POS and ATM authorization-only and full financial message transactions, including preauthorization messages. The acquirer must use messages consistent within a transaction set. V.I.P. enforces these rules by comparing an incoming message with previous messages containing the same key data elements. In general, V.I.P. rejects messages out of context or out of sequence. V.I.P. assigns reject code 0514 if the response message cannot be matched with the request. VisaNet performs consistency editing to prevent invalid, out-of-context messages from being sent to an issuer.
Message Matching Table – Key Data Fields
V.I.P. uses the following key data fields to match requests and responses and to identify repeat or duplicate requests:

Field 32 – Acquiring Institution Identification Code Field 37 – Retrieval Reference Number Field 41 – Card Acceptor Terminal Identification Field 42 – Card Acceptor Identification Code Field 63.1 – Network Identification Code

Acquirers must exercise caution if reusing field 37 values when submitting authorization requests. The first four digits of Field 37 must contain a valid Julian date in the yddd format, where the first digit = 0–9 and the next three digits = 001–366. V.I.P. can also use other message fields, such as Field 7 – Transmission Date and Time and Field 11 – System Trace Audit Number to link messages, although the system does not retain them in the message matching table. The message matching table retains a transaction’s key field information until the issuer or STIP sends a response to that transaction. Certain card type transactions require the message matching table not restore values from certain fields when those values differ between the request and the response, for instance, when the amount in field 4 in the response to certain private-label requests is different from the amount in field 4 in its corresponding original request.

Field 62.2 – Transaction Identifier is a key field for message identification and matching. V.I.P. assigns a TID to all transactions. V.I.P. assigns a TID to all 0100 authorizations, 0200 full financial requests, 0120 and 0220 STIP advices. V.I.P. returns the TID to acquirers in 0110, 0130, 0210, and 0230 responses. Field 62.2 is mandatory in 0400 reversals (including partial reversals) and 0420 reversal advices. V.I.P. returns this field in 0410 and 0430 responses even if the issuer does not include it in the response. This field is also present in 0220 dispute response financials, 0282 dispute response financial status advices, 0422 dispute financials, 0432 dispute financial responses, and in dispute financial reversals and their responses. V.I.P. does not send field 62.2 to gateway issuers. V.I.P. returns this field to acquirers in gateway response messages.

A transaction set cannot include invalid transactions. For instance, a purchase transaction set cannot include a merchandise return. A transaction cannot be processed with invalid system transactions. For instance, an authorization cannot be processed with a dispute financial or dispute response financial. In addition, the function of a response must correspond to the function of the request. For instance, a reversal response to a purchase request is not valid.

Within a transaction set, transactions must be processed in a logical sequence. For instance, in a purchase or a merchandise return transaction set containing an adjustment, the original purchase or merchandise return must precede the adjustment.

Within a transaction set, all messages requiring an account number must contain the same account number. If the first message in a transaction set contains an account number, the same account number must be used in all subsequent messages requiring an account number.

The value in Field 4 – Amount, Transaction must be identical in all request and response pairs requiring an amount. All transactions within a transaction set must contain the same transaction amount except for dispute financials, dispute response financials, and adjustments. Dispute response financials of transactions must be for the same amount as for the original transaction or dispute financial.

A duplicate message has the same message type and key data elements (acquiring institution ID, retrieval reference number, trace number, and transaction identifier) as a prior message. V.I.P. processes duplicates as follows:

If processing of the original request was completed (a response was sent), V.I.P. responds to the acquirer with response code 94 (duplicate transmission) in field 39 and, optionally, includes the original response value in field 44.11. In this case, V.I.P. does not involve STIP nor the issuer. V.I.P. logs the request and the response. For duplicate transactions from authorization-only acquirers to full service issuers, V.I.P. sends the field 39 response code and t
he field 38 authorization code from the original.
If processing of the original request is still in progress, V.I.P. logs the duplicate and discards it. (V.I.P. assumes the original will be completed; therefore the duplicate is not needed.)

Issuers must not use a response code value of 94 in response messages. If upon a time-out, an acquirer chooses to retry the authorization request, it must generate a repeat or a reversal. Repeats are not allowed for full service POS transactions. If authorization-only acquirers send 0101 POS request message 10 seconds after the original message has been processed, full service issuers will receive 0101 request messages. Acquirers should ensure their merchants know to re-swipe the cardholder's card when resubmitting an authorization request after the previous request has been reversed.

Full service acquirers and issuers must establish an in-house processing center or must designate another center or third-party processor to perform the necessary processing functions. Issuer and acquirer country codes Card type, for instance, Visa card Card program, for instance, Classic or Platinum Whether to block purchase transactions, cash transactions, or both Whether cards are valid in all countries, valid only in the issuing country, valid in countries identified in the table for the issuing identifier, or invalid in countries identified in the table for the issuing identifier.

A purchase transaction is a standard purchase request to authorize, post, and settle a transaction involving the sale of goods or services. Purchase transactions are supported by Visa POS.

Cashback transactions for Visa are included in the flows for this category. A purchase with cashback transaction differs from a purchase by the presence of an amount in Field 61 61.1—Other Amounts. A purchase with cashback transaction is a variation of the purchase transaction that permits the cardholder to get cash in addition to goods or services. For Visa, purchase with cashback is allowed for domestic transactions only; it is not supported for international transactions. Participating regions may offer a cashback service through VisaNet. Clients can contact their Visa representatives for information about availability. Visa cashback transactions are only allowed in face-to-face POS environments. This transaction is optional for acquirers and for merchants. Merchants that want to support this transaction service establish their own cashback limits. For full service participants outside of the United Kingdom (U.K.), Field 4—Amount, Transaction must contain the total transaction amount, which is the sum of the purchase amount and the cashback amount. For the U.K., a purchase with cashback transaction differs from a purchase by an amount in Field 61.1, positions 1–12—Other Amount, Transaction. Regional Visa Rules can apply to cashback transactions. Keeping the cashback amount separate from the purchase amount allows the issuer to check the desired cashback amount against daily cash withdrawal limits, which may differ from daily purchase limits. If the desired cashback amount causes the daily cash withdrawal limit to be exceeded, or if the combined purchase and cashback amount exceeds the cardholder's available balance but the purchase amount alone does not, the issuer can decline the transaction by using a response code to indicate that the cashback limit was exceeded, and the merchant can send a new transaction for the purchase amount only. A manual cash disbursement is a transaction by which the cardholder obtains cash in a face-to-face environment. It is valid for Visa POS. Purchase requests and manual cash disbursements have financial impact on cardholder accounts. They result in the updating of system settlement totals for the acquirer and issuer. A previously approved authorization (0100) or financial transaction (0200) is cancelled at the point of service because:
The cardholder does not complete the transaction. The merchant makes an error that requires voiding.

Issuers use a dispute financial transaction to return a previously accepted financial transaction to an acquirer. Issuers have the right to charge back to the acquirer posted transactions that are disputed by the cardholder or are identified as invalid by the issuer. Dispute financials must adhere to applicable Visa Core Rules and Visa Product and Service Rules. Dispute financials must be submitted within a set number of calendar days from the origination date of the transaction being disputed. The set number of days varies by the type of dispute financial and is within 45 to 180 calendar days of the original transaction. The dispute financial amount should be for the original amount and should not include optional issuer fees. Partial dispute financials are allowed when the cleared amount exceeds the authorized amount. The issuer has the option of entering dispute financials using Visa Resolve Online (VROL). The acquirer can choose to receive dispute financials through VROL. The dispute financial flows from the issuer to the acquirer—the opposite direction from other financial transactions. The response by the acquirer acknowledges that it successfully received and processed the dispute financial. The response does not signify that the acquirer is in agreement with the request. Acquirers use dispute response financials to return invalid dispute financials.

If the dispute financial times out at the issuer, the issuer should resend the dispute financial transaction unchanged. A fee-related transaction is a fee collection or a funds disbursement transaction. Clients use this transaction to collect or to remit miscellaneous fees such as recovered card rewards. These advices contain all of the information needed for settlement. Visa Resolve Online (VROL) supports 0220 and 0422 fee messages. Fee transactions usually do not relate directly to cardholder transactions, and therefore usually do not result in postings to cardholders' accounts. They are financial in nature, however, and they

update settlement totals for the sender and for the receiver. Because fee-related transactions do not require authorization and cannot be declined, they are always processed as advice message types. The value in Field 3— 3—Processing Code of a fee collection must be 19xxxx. The value in field 3 of a funds disbursement must be 29xxxx. Clients use these values to distinguish fee-related transactions from other transactions with the same message types. For acquirer-initiated, fee-related transactions, the acquirer sends an 0220 fee-related advice to the issuer, and the issuer acknowledges with an 0230 advice response. V.I.P. accepts free-text messages for the destination client when the destination is unavailable. The system stores an 0620 advice in the advice queue for recovery by the destination client. rvice, refer to V.I.P. System Services.

The following fields in the 0800 request are used for a DKE Service key exchange request: Field 11 11—System Trace Audit Number Field 33 33—Forwarding Institution Identification Code Field 39 39—Response Code Field 48, U
sage 14 14—Dynamic Key Exchange Working Key Check Value
Field 52 52—Personal Identification Number (PIN) Data Field 53 53—Security-Related Control Information Field 63.1—Net

The 0800 message initiator, which can be a participating acquirer or issuer, or V.I.P., assigns the trace number (in field 11). Clients must return the trace number unchanged in the 0810 response. V.I.P. continues sending messages with the old key until it receives the 0810 response. Therefore, single-key issuers must keep a copy of the old key until V.I.P. begins using the new one. If V.I.P. encounters PIN block errors during standard message processing, V.I.P. returns response code 81 (cryptographic error found) in PIN in the 0800 request and initiates an automatic acquirer key change. If the issuer encounters a PIN block error during verification, it returns response code

in the 0810 response. V.I.P. initiates an automatic issuer working key change. V.I.P. has a 10-second time-out for all dynamic key exchange messages containing new working keys. Multicurrency support is required for all full service POS and ATM acquirers and issuers except those whose cardholder billing currency and settlement currency are United States (U.S.) dollars. V.I.P. features full multicurrency support for international POS and ATM transactions. The Multicurrency Service includes:

Automatic conversion from the transaction currency to the currency of the cardholder's account. Automatic conversion from the transaction currency to the acquirer's settlement currency (if the two are different). Automatic conversion from the currency of the cardholder's account to the issuer's settlement currency (if the two are different).

The transaction currency is generally the currency of the country in which a transaction takes place. The cardholder billing currency is generally the currency of the country in which the account is domiciled. Full financial messages contain several multicurrency fields supporting the various amounts involved in currency exchange calculation. These fields contain the following data:
The transaction amount in the transaction currency The transaction amount in the cardholder billing currency The settlement amount
The conversion rates The date of the conversion rate table used by V.I.P.

Participating clients receive these standard multicurrency fields in their online messages, reports, and raw data. For non-participating clients, transaction and settlement amounts appear in online messages, raw data, and reports in U.S. dollars only. Non-participating clients that migrate to the Multicurrency Service have the advantage of using the additional information.
V.I.P. determines applicable currencies for a given transaction as follows:

The acquirer indicates the transaction amount and the transaction currency in the request message. V.I.P. determines the issuer's currencies based on the first several digits of the primary account number (PAN), which is read from the magnetic stripe on the card used for the transaction. These initial digits, called the issuing identifier, are used to locate issuer-supplied data, including the cardholder billing currency and the issuer's settlement currency, on V.I.P. databases. V.I.P. determines the acquirer's settlement currency based on the acquirer ID in the request message. This ID is used to locate acquirer-supplied data on V.I.P. databases.

V.I.P. supports transaction and cardholder billing currencies recognized by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO). Some of these currencies are also supported as settlement currencies. For the current list of supported currencies, see Full Service POS Online Messages Technical Specifications, and Full Service ATM Online Messages Technical Specifications.
VisaNet uses buy and sell rates for currency conversion. VisaNet pairs these rates into:

USD-based rates that are used when converting non-USD currencies against the U.S. dollar. Cross rates (non-USD-based rates) that VisaNet use for selected currencies for which the rates quoted are against a currency other than the U.S. dollar.
The Multicurrency Chapter in V.I.P. System Services, contains a complete description of the currency conversion process and examples of currency conversion.

Visa determines the wholesale rate five days a week (Monday through Friday) based on the cost to Visa of buying and selling currencies on the foreign exchange markets: These cross border charges vary by region. Refer to the Visa Rules for more information. Issuers can choose to charge an optional issuer fee to the cardholder for transactions that require currency conversion. The issuer can specify an intraregional or interregional optional issuer fee, or can specify both. VisaNet maintains the optional issuer fee, which may be a mark-up or a rebate, in V.I.P. databases according to issuing identifiers. VisaNet calculates this optional fee at the time of currency conversion using the percentage rate the issuer establishes. To implement an optional issuer currency conversion fee, the client must contact Visa. All VisaNet systems that support Multicurrency Service processing use common conversion rates. V.I.P. performs currency conversion in calculating settlement amounts when the acquirer's settlement currency is not the same as the transaction currency, or when the issuer's settlement currency is not the same as the cardholder billing currency. There is no settlement amount for non-financial transactions. However, for balance inquiries, VisaNet will calculate and settle the balance inquiry interchange reimbursement fee for clients. V.I.P. supports an XML-only message to convert an amount and return the results to the Mobile gateway. The XML currency conversion request message contains a “source” Primary Account Number (PAN), a ”destination” PAN, an amount, and a processing code. V.I.P. looks up the currencies associated with the source PAN and the destination PAN. It uses the source currency as the transaction currency and associates it with the amount submitted. V.I.P. performs a conversion of the amount and source currency to the destination cardholder billing using the conversion rates associated with the transaction type as specified by the processing code.

The transaction amount and the currency code (USD$100) The cardholder billing amount and the currency code (AU$126.56) The settlement amount and the currency code (AU$125.00)

Raw data identifies the optional issuer fee and the optional issuer ISA amount. When an issuer is not available, V.I.P. acts as a backup processor and authorizes or declines transactions on the issuer's behalf. This V.I.P. function is referred to as Stand-In Processing, or STIP. All issuers must specify the STIP parameters used to process transactions when they are unable to respond. These parameters ensure cardholder approval rates in STIP are consistent with approval rates when the issuer responds. STIP approval rates must meet or exceed the minimum approval rates defined in the Visa rules for the product type. STIP is not available for Mastercard transactions regardless of region.
When an acquirer is not available to receive issuer generated transactions, such as dispute financials, STIP acts as a backup processor and accepts the transactions on the acquirer's behalf.
STIP processes authorization requests (0100s), financial requests (0200s), reversal requests (0400s), and reversal advices (0420s) destined for an issuer under the following conditions:

The line to the issuer is not available. The issuer is signed off. The issuer is in Advice Recovery-only mode. The issuer does not respond within a specified time limit. When the time limit for the client to respond expires, the expiration triggers Assured Transaction Response (ATR) and V.I.P. invokes STIP. The transaction is an address verification-only request for an issuer that participates in Visa Secure (formerly known as Verified by Visa (VbV)). For information about Visa Secure Electronic Commerce (VSEC) With Visa Secure, see V.I.P. System Services. The request is a preauthorization or preauthorization completion and the STIP advice of the original has not been recovered by the issuer.

The Assured Transaction Response (ATR) function monitors all authorization requests it forwards to issuers to ensure that each request receives a timely authorization response. When V.I.P. routes a request to the issuer, it sets a timer to monitor how long the issuer takes to respond. If an issuer does not send an authorization response to V.I.P. within the specified time limit, V.I.P. will invoke STIP to determine the approval or decline decision on the issuer’s behalf. If an issuer sends a response after V.I.P. has diverted the corresponding request to STIP, the STIP-generated decision prevails, and V.I.P. discards the response from the issuer. PACM protects issuers against periods of excessive message volume by ensuring that their processing capacity is available for transactions with the greatest customer service and risk control implications. When the volume of request messages exceeds the issuer's processing capacity, PACM routes a calculated number of low-risk transactions to STIP for the next 60 seconds. This diversion to STIP enables issuers to process higher-risk financial transactions, which reduces risk. PACM enables issuers to provide higher levels of customer service by reducing the frequency of inappropriate declines. PACM checks transaction volume every 60 seconds and adjusts the number of transactions it routes to STIP so that the optimum number of messages can be processed by the issuer without exceeding the issuer's capacity. In reversals, debit processing codes decrease the totals, while credit processing codes increase the totals. For a description of Field 3—Processing Code, refer to the V.I.P. System technical specifications manuals. Activity counts and amounts are never reduced to less than zero. If a credit adjustment exceeds the activity totals, STIP resets the activity record to zero.

Reversals cannot be declined. When STIP receives a reversal, it always approves the reversal and creates an advice for the issuer. STIP, however, edits the reversal for validity. STIP checks the reversal for proper syntax and consistency, and searches for the corresponding original transaction being reversed. If STIP finds the original transaction, STIP updates the activity records, and the reversal has financial impact. If STIP does not find the financial record, the reversal has no financial impact so STIP does not update the activity records. The issuer may still receive response code 00 (approved) or the acquirer may receive response code 21 (no action taken). V.I.P. generates a reversal for the issuer if STIP cannot deliver an 0210 response to an approved 0200 request to the acquirer. STIP also generates reversals to the issuer for returned responses or for late responses to approved requests. STIP responds with response code 79 (already reversed) if an acquirer sends a reversal and the history record shows that a previous reversal was processed for the same transaction. This response code value is only used by V.I.P. Issuers must not use this value in response messages.

STIP responds with response code 80 (no financial impact) if an acquirer sends a reversal and the history records show that the original request was declined. STIP responds with response code 76 (unsolicited reversal) if there is no history for the transaction in question and the reversal is inter-VIC, or if V.I.P. is in single-center mode.

When STIP approves a reversal, it updates the cardholder's activity record if the reversal has settlement impact. For instance, STIP decreases POS counts and amounts for a valid reversal of a purchase transaction. STIP also decreases the cardholder's grand totals accordingly. When a reversal has a credit effect on the cardholder's account, activity counts and amounts on file are never set to less than zero.

Preauthorization Stand-In Service is an optional service for Interlink issuers that do not have the system capabilities to process preauthorization requests and preauthorization completions. When an issuer participates in this service, V.I.P. stands in for all preauthorization request and completion transactions, and assigns STIP reason code 9032 to Subfield 63.4—STIP/Switch Reason Code of each transaction to indicate that it was processed by the service.

The preauthorization limit indicates the maximum amount that can be approved for preauthorization transactions processed by the Preauthorization Stand-In Service. The designated maximum amount for this limit is on a per-transaction basis, unlike the basic activity limits, which are cumulative throughout the day. Interlink issuers that participate in the Preauthorization Stand-In Service are required to select a value for the preauthorization limit. In addition to the basic activity limits, all issuers must specify a preauthorization limit. The preauthorization limit can be a different value from that set for the basic activity limits.

For a preauthorization request to receive a full approval when processed by this service, the request must pass all of the standard STIP editing tests described earlier in this chapter. In addition, the transaction request amount must not exceed the amount specified as the issuer's preauthorization limit. V.I.P. issues a partial approval if:

The preauthorization request passes all STIP editing tests except the activity check. The full preauthorization amount requested exceeds basic activity limits or exceeds the preauthorization limit set by the issuer—but a lesser, non-zero amount would be within the limits. This partial approval amount is the greatest amount possible without exceeding the limits.

The Card Verification Value (CVV) Service is a POS and ATM risk control service that protects issuers and acquirers from fraud losses associated with counterfeit Visa cards. The CVV is a unique value calculated from data encoded on the magnetic stripe using the Data Encryption Standard (DES) algorithm. The Integrated Chip Card card verification value (iCVV) is a unique value calculated from data encoded on the chip image using the DES algorithm. The Dynamic Card Verification Value (dCVV) is a unique value calculated from the data encoded on the chip in a contactless transaction. The CVV Service refers to the Visa verification service available through the VisaNet Integrated Payment (V.I.P.) System. The CVV Service processes CVVs and iCVVs. Participation in the CVV Service is mandatory for issuers of all Visa card products, including Visa Electron. Issuers in the AP and CEMEA regions must use default CVV processing options where Visa validates the CVV and declines transactions that failed CVV validation with the issuer selected response code. Using iCVVs is mandatory for chip card issuers. Using dCVVs is optional for contactless card issuers. Acquirers of all Visa card products must provide complete, unaltered magnetic stripe data (from the magnetic stripe or from the chip) in 0100 authorization messages and in 0200 financial messages.
The CVV Service allows issuers to detect invalid cards by checking the content on a card's magnetic stripe or its chip image.

The CVV resides on the magnetic stripe on the back of the card. Visa Smart Debit/Smart Credit (VSDC) chip cards have a magnetic stripe and a chip, which contains an image of the magnetic stripe data. VSDC cards can contain the same CVV values on its magnetic stripe and on its magnetic stripe image (MSI) on the chip. At the issuer's option, the value of the CVV (on Track 2 of the magnetic stripe) and that in the chip image's CVV can be different. In this case, the MSI contains an iCVV.

The contents on the magnetic stripe and in the chip are identical, unless the chip contains an iCVV. Having one verification value for the magnetic stripe (CVV) and a different one for the chip image (iCVV) causes CVV validation to fail if chip information has been used to create a fraudulent magnetic stripe.

The Card Verification Value 2 (CVV2) Service is a card verification tool designed to reduce fraud losses on transactions when the card is present and when the card is not present. The service confirms that a genuine Visa card is used during the transaction. The CVV2 Service is available to issuers and acquirers in all Visa regions. All Visa cards (including emergency replacement cards) issued in the U.S. region must carry the CVV2 security number. Issuers indent-print a 3-digit CVV2 on the back of a Visa card using a reverse italic font. Issuers generate the CVV2 values using Data Encryption Standard (DES) keys and an algorithm. The encrypted value is based on the primary account number, the card's expiration date, a

zero service code. Participating merchants manually enter the CVV2 numeric value for validation by V.I.P., the issuer, or both. V.I.P., the issuer, or both, verif y the CVV2 and return the CVV2 result code to the merchant. If V.I.P. performs the validation, the Visa Security Module (VSM) verifies the CVV2 before it passes the authorization request to the issuer or to STIP. Issuers can choose to have V.I.P. check the CVV2 in all CVV2-eligible authorization requests. To validate the CVV2, V.I.P. uses the DES key and other CVV2 parameters provided by participating issuers to calculate the CVV2 value and compare it to the card's printed CVV2. If V.I.P. or the issuer generates a CVV2 “no match” result, V.I.P. assigns CVV2 Result Code N—No Match to the transaction. V.I.P. forwards the result to the issuer. The issuer optionally may recheck the CVV2 and return another CVV2 result code or can rely solely on the V.I.P. CVV2 result and return the CVV2 result code along with the response code. Although a CVV2 value is never passed in ATM or in Interlink transactions, issuers of Interlink and ATM cards (including Plus cards) can optionally use CVV2s for purposes of card activation, address

changes, voice response unit (VRU) cardholder validation, and other bank customer service options to ensure that the cardholder has the genuine card in hand. The CAVV is a cryptographic value generated by the issuer and sent to the merchant during the authentication process in a Visa Secure transaction. The verification process involves two phases: 1.

During the Visa Secure phase, the issuer or V.I.P. electronically identifies the cardholder and generates a CAVV that is associated with the purchase or financial transaction. When V.I.P. processes financial transactions, it delivers them for account posting in real time using 02xx and 04xx messages. Clearing is the process of collecting an individual transaction from one client or processor and delivering it to another. Clearing also includes the calculation of fees and charges. Settlement is the process of calculating and determining the net financial position of each client for all transactions that are cleared.

The result of this process is a net settlement value for each settlement endpoint and the production of daily settlement reports. A key aspect of the clearing process is valuation, which includes the calculation of many types of fees and charges. The clearing system calculates all of these values—for instance, fees, charges, and discounts. VSS, described in the next section, does not perform valuation. VSS reports transactions processed through the clearing system— BASE II and V.I.P. transactions. VSS aggregates settlement advices created by the clearing system into a net settlement position at the end of the cycle.

Chapter 11 Considerations for Visa POS Issuers
This chapter is intended for full service clients that issue Visa cards. These issuers have special processing considerations, which this chapter describes.

Visa POS acquirers can choose to send transactions using the full service or the authorization-only processing method. The authorization-only acquirer sends above-floor-limit POS transactions made with a Visa POS card as authorization requests (0100s). One to several days later, the acquirer submits BASE II clearing records (TC 05s and TC 06s). V.I.P. clears these BASE II records to full service issuers as deferred clearing advices (0220s), messages similar to the online deferred clearing advices. As a result, Visa POS issuers that choose to process transactions using the full service method must be prepared to receive online financial transactions from full service acquirers, and to receive authorization messages followed by deferred clearing transactions from full service and authorization-only acquirers. For authorization-only acquired POS transactions, the full service issuer must be prepared to accept authorization requests (0100s) that have no financial impact. The full service issuer may choose to manage the cardholder's available balance or credit line by placing a temporary hold on funds until it receives the 0220 advice. Because there could be circumstances in which the issuer does not receive

the 0220 advice (for instance, a reversal was not properly processed), the full service issuer may want to establish an expiration date for holds, possibly three to four days after the authorization date. Another consideration for full service issuers is that for cross-currency transactions from authorization-only acquirers, the cardholder billing amount in the 0220 message may be different from the amount authorized. This difference may be due to fluctuations in currency conversion rates between the date of the authorization and the date that the transaction clears. Full service issuers also need to remember that acquirers may not know the final amount at the time of authorization and that some transactions may not have required an authorization because they were below the floor limit.

Occasionally, client-initiated transactions fail to process as anticipated; for instance, V.I.P. might reject a request because of an invalid field value. Clients' Visa representatives can help resolve such problems.
